newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee crop may fall 20 pct - agronomist.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee crop may fall 20 pct - agronomist.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could see a fall of 20 percent on the 1996/97 harvest, according to preliminary soundings by an agronomist at the Sao Paulo state Institute of Agricultural Economics.

"The preliminary information we have is there will be around a 20 percent drop from this year's levels," said Luiz Moricochi. "The question is a 20 percent drop from what as there are various figures for the 1996/97 harvest but I would say that this year's crop was around 24 million bags."
Moricochi based his forecast on conversations with agronomists and growers throughout the key coffee growing regions in Brazil.
"But this is only preliminary data. Only in January and February will we have a clear idea of size," he said.

Moricochi is responsible for co-ordinating forecasts for the state of Sao Paulo, with the institute currently conducting surveys for the 1997/98 harvest in the state which should be ready in December.
"This year we saw production of 3.19 million bags against 1.8 million in 1995. But next year I think we should see a fall here in the state also of around 20 percent," he said.
